extracted.intended_audience: horror writers, publishers, booksellers, librarians, and HWA members
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Horror Writers Association's award categories and the standards used to recognize achievement in horror writing and related contributions (annual Bram Stoker Awards, lifetime achievement, specialty press, volunteer service).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Bram Stoker Awards (superior achievement in horror writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented annually for superior achievement in horror writing in twelve different categories; a well-recognized guide to the best new horror literature and film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual awards across a range of categories (twelve) recognizing 'superior achievement' in horror; positions the awards as a guide to outstanding new horror writing and film. No further scoring details provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Bram Stoker Award for Lifetime Achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented periodically to an individual whose work has substantially influenced the horror genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded for substantial influence on the genre; while often presented to a writer, it may also be given for influential accomplishments in other creative fields. No nomination/scoring mechanics given here.

rubrics_metrics.name: The HWA Specialty Press Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented periodically to a small or specialty publisher who has made an outstanding contribution to Horror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets small or specialty presses; criterion is an 'outstanding contribution' to the horror field (publishing). No further examples or scoring rubrics on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: HWA Volunteer Service Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented on an occasional basis to one of the many dedicated member volunteers who make HWA possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes significant volunteer service to the organization; aimed at dedicated members whose work supports HWA activities. Page gives no detailed nomination or evaluation procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of contributions beyond writing
rubrics_metrics.description: HWA acknowledges that horror is more than good writing and recognizes the roles of publishers, booksellers, librarians, and volunteers in supporting dark literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion that contributions to the health of the field (publishing, selling, recommending, volunteering) are award-worthy; examples listed include publishers, librarians, booksellers, and generous volunteers. No formalized metrics provided on this page.
